questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The opportunity to live in a different culture in contrast to ours, exploring their perspective on the world. Furthermore I wanted to improve my Spanish.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: 9 out 10, because the educational level is pretty low, but the experience is wild.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: KU is not helping you that much, so you need to put a good amount of time in finding out things on you own. You can try to write to the university’s international office, but they are also a bit slow. But in the end is not so bad, it just take some time.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Udlap have a well functioning International office, which have a lot of things planned for you in the beginning. Tours in the campus and of the area. They help you with all the practical stuff.

You will experience that the local students are really welcoming, so you can always just ask them for help. People are so friendly and easy to talk to.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: A lot of information, but they are a bit slow to answer.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Don’t live at Campus. It’s more expensive and restricted, because of security guards, checklist and opening hours for visitors. I met some who liked it, but I would personally not.

Outside the campus you pay around 1000 kr. pr. Month. I lived with a housing company called Travelslife, which had nice housing. Choose housing in Casa Santa Fe or Casa Iguana. I lived in Casa Iguana, and it was really good. Huge rooftop terraza, with view of the volcano and pyramid. Don,t there the housing close to the school. It’s kind of shit.

But Oswaldo (+52 222 134 1794, WhatsApp number) who is in control of the organization is a special guy, but have some fine housing. Search on travels_life_mexico on insta.

Their is also another housing organization called Cholula Capital, you could try out.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Don’t do it haha.  Ut as mentioned, some people liked it, fx because of the extra security. But Cholula is a really save city as most of Mexico is.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived with a lot of international students, who I travelled with later. It was so good. Oswaldo was the only minus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It doesn’t really make any sense, because their course catalogue is based on previous years, so you can end up signing in for a course, which they don’t provide in your semester. Furthermore is there only written 1 to 3 lines about the course, so it’s impossible to know what you sign up for. When you make your pre approval, show KU that they don’t have that much information about the courses. Then KU would approve it or say that you need to contact the profesor. In the beginning of the semester, the profesor will upload all the information you need.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Can’t really remember, sry. But UDLAP will send you a guide to what to do.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could contact the international office and the professors, but it’s kind of slow.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Fivtyfivty

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
My advice would be just choose some courses who seem interesting before leaving. Then in the first couple of weeks of the semester is possible to shuffle courses, and resend a pre approval to KU.

A smart trick is to try laying all your courses on two days, because the you have the possibility of traveling or party longer in the weekends whiteout being absence from uni.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The level of some course are high and others really low. I only choose English courses, but I think the Spanish courses are of higher level.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It varies a lot. Most of the English courses were relatively easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is a Gymnasie wibe, with small classroom and the teacher standing at the board. A classroom is typically max. 30 people.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Geopolitics and strategic analysis, great teacher named Guy. Choose some courses with him, if you can.

International Relations Theory, with Guy

Political and Social Theory, with Dolores. Not that good, but fine enough.

Zoology, with Paul. Great teacher, but a random course I took for fun. 

Econometrics and another political course, which I chose to drop in the begging.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The courses with Guy and Paul. Furthermore I heard about some nice courses in statistics and environmental governance.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *

Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Only to the guy who is organizing the housing. You sign a contact in the beginning, which say you have to pay for min. 5 months. I only livet there for 4 months. If you choose him, try to ask him in the beginning why you have to pay for it. He is interested in renting out, so you could easily pressure him a bit. 

I bought a bike and sold it again after the semester. Really with it, instead of taking Ubers to things far away.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Buying food to cook yourself was a bit expensive relatively to what Mexicans are paid in average.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I didn’t really attend more than one time to their trips or courses. They have a lot of possibilities, but you find the same outside where it’s more fun and less expensive.

Buuuuut there sports facilities are really good. Tennis courts, basketball, outside pool, free giant fitness, football pitches. Really, really good facilities. We bought some rackets and played a lot of tennis. 

You can also join fx the football team, which could be a good way of meeting new people.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Language, music and different sports. They made some trips outside also.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
They’re sports facilities. Also go watch their university team in American Football, it’s for free and a good atmosphere.

I had a great Spanish teacher, Karla. WhatsApp number +52 222 461 4010. She also studies at the uni.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Important. Remember to chill and explore Cholula, so you don't get stressed of going on weekend trips all the time. I needed to have a bit of daily life, which is also really cool to try out, because the mood and the people are just different compared to at home.

But when that is said.

Smaller weekend trips in the “close” area could be walking around in Puebla and Mexico City, which are beutiful cities. In Mexico City I really enjoyed going the area Roma Norte and Condeasa, but just go around and get a bit lost. So many nice places. 

Climbing Malinche and Izta if you are real mountaineer. There is also a really good hike around the National center between the active volcano Popo and the mountain Izta. Malinche and the hike between Izta you can do whiteout a guide, but going on top of Izta you need a guide.

Go to the local football stadium in Puebla. Really nice, when they play against Club America. 

Bike around Cholula and up in the hills. Some good mountain biking.

A cool cactus park and so rounding mountains called Jardín Zapotitlan. We camped in the park in a tent for two days. Really nice waking up surrounded by cactus and mountains.

Eat your way through their amazing food.

Trips longer away, which was really nice: Baja California, El Cheppe (tourist train) and the cities on the tracks (especially Barrancas de Cobre is breathtaking), Oxaca (Puerto Escondido), Ciapas and Yucatán. But here you need a week or more, which is possible during the semester. The professors are sweet and know you are an exchange student.

If you are there in the autum semester you have Dia de Muertos, which is really nice in Oxaca and Michoacán. In the winter there should be a nature phenomenon with butterflies, Mariposas Monarca.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Culture shock is the way they are thinking about time, which can be annoying, but also really stress free and more chilled.

The weather in Cholula gets cold during winter. It’s on a mountain range so the temperature differs a lot during the day. Cold in the morning, the warm and cold again during the night. A bit like Denmark, just bigger differences in heat because of the mountains. Rains season means a lot of water every day, but only for a couple of hours, then it get sunny.

Don’t drink the water.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They will come to you. They are really open and welcoming to exchange students. Otherwise join a sports team at the uni.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The idea of time.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The wibe is really good. Warm, happy and festive people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Remember to chill in the city, don’t always go on weekend trips. Be open to meet the locals and your costudents. 

Buy a bike 

Remember warm cloth and a rain jacket. When you fly you can always have one check in bag, a hand luggage and a personal item, which could be a backpack. You can always store some of your luggage, with some sweet people in Cholula, when you go traveling after the semester. Ofc. if you want to leave from Mexico.

Choose one of the housing organizations.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy it, it’s gonna be really nice even though it can seem a bit scary in the beginning.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting the people and their vibe and perspective on the world. Having a break from uni at home and learning a new language.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: During all the recruitments and pre approval for the universities.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
